methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $200M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Sublime Systems, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Leah Ellis and Yet-Ming Chiang, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company operating in the same sector. The peer set includes later-stage entities such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy, reflecting the competitive landscape in frontier climate technology.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the company's $200M+ total raised as a proxy base value and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $380M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yielded a median valuation of $1.0B, with observed peer valuations ranging from $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals). These peers represent Series C entities, introducing stage-related upward bias to the median.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $323M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $690M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in stage progression velocity within frontier energy, as well as substantial valuation variance among peer companies despite sector and stage proximity. The peer-median estimate sits above stage-progression by a factor of 2.6x, suggesting either that comparable companies have achieved disproportionate investor confidence or that typical Series B-to-next-stage multiples may understate frontier-tech progression in favorable market conditions. Resolution of this gap depends on capital deployment timeline and technical validation outcomes.
